wrong_comments.submittal_quote: The supply air temperature loop is enabled only while the supply fan is proven on. When it is disabled, heating is off and the economizer is at minimum position.
wrong_comments.spec_quote: The supply air temperature control loop shall be enabled when the supply fan is proven on; otherwise the loop shall be disabled with heating off and the economizer at minimum position.
wrong_comments.reason: The submittal states the loop is enabled *only* when the supply fan is on, while the specification states it is disabled with heating off and the economizer at minimum position when the supply fan is not proven on.

wrong_comments.submittal_quote: In the Occupied and Setup modes the supply air temperature setpoint is 55 °F with outdoor air at 70 °F or warmer and rises linearly to the maximum setpoint with outdoor air at 60 °F or cooler.
wrong_comments.spec_quote: During Occupied and Setup modes the supply air temperature setpoint shall be reset from 55 °F when the outdoor air temperature is 70 °F and above, proportionally up to the maximum supply air temperature setpoint when the outdoor air temperature is 60 °F and below.
wrong_comments.reason: The submittal states a linear rise from 55°F to the maximum setpoint, while the specification states a proportional reset.

wrong_comments.submittal_quote: Economizer operation is locked out above an outdoor air temperature of 75 °F and released once the outdoor air temperature drops 1 °F below the limit.
wrong_comments.spec_quote: The economizer shall be disabled when the outdoor air temperature exceeds 75 °F and enabled again when it falls 1 °F below that limit.
wrong_comments.reason: The submittal states the economizer is locked out above 75°F and released when it drops 1°F, while the specification states it is disabled above 75°F and re-enabled when it drops 1°F. This is a different trigger.

wrong_comments.submittal_quote: Stage 1: when supply air temperature stays below 40 °F for 5 minutes, the controller sends two heating hot water plant requests, holds the outdoor air damper at minimum position and modulates the heating coil to maintain at least 42 °F; stage 1 ends after the supply air temperature is above 45 °F for 5 minutes.
wrong_comments.spec_quote: If the supply air temperature drops below 40 °F for 5 minutes, the controller shall send two heating hot water plant requests, override the outdoor air damper to minimum position, and modulate the heating coil to keep the supply air temperature at or above 42 °F; this stage shall end when the supply air temperature is above 45 °F for 5 minutes.
wrong_comments.reason: The submittal states the outdoor air damper is held at minimum position, while the specification states it is overridden to minimum position. This is a different action.

wrong_comments.submittal_quote: The freeze-stat is hardwired in the fan starter circuits and stops the supply and return fans independent of the BAS; the BAS monitors its status.
wrong_comments.spec_quote: The freeze-stat shall be hardwired to stop the supply and return fans regardless of the BAS command, and its status shall be monitored by the BAS.
wrong_comments.reason: The submittal states the freeze-stat stops the fans independently of the BAS, while the specification states the BAS monitors its status, creating a contradiction in the control logic.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.1.1 Each zone holds 21.7 °C heating and 24.4 °C cooling when occupied and 15.6 °C heating and 29.4 °C cooling when unoccupied.
comments.spec_quote: 3.1.1 Occupied zone setpoints shall be 71 °F heating and 76 °F cooling; unoccupied setpoints shall be 60 °F heating and 85 °F cooling.
comments.reason: The submittal specifies 21.7 °C and 24.4 °C for occupied zones, which is significantly different from the specification’s 71 °F and 76 °F.  This represents a conversion error.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.1.2 Occupants may adjust the zone setpoints by at most 1.1 °C in either direction.
comments.spec_quote: 3.1.2 Occupant adjustment of the zone setpoints shall be limited to plus or minus 2 °F.
comments.reason: The submittal specifies a maximum adjustment of 1.1 °C, while the specification requires a maximum adjustment of 2 °F. This represents a conversion error.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.3.1 As the cooling loop rises from 0 to 100 percent, the airflow setpoint falls from the maximum cooling airflow to the minimum.
comments.spec_quote: 3.3.1 In cooling, the airflow setpoint shall be reset from the minimum airflow up to the maximum cooling airflow as the cooling loop rises from 0 to 100 percent.
comments.reason: The submittal states the airflow decreases from maximum cooling to minimum, while the specification states it increases from minimum to maximum.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.3.2 From 0 to 50 percent heating loop the discharge air temperature setpoint rises from zone temperature to 11.1 °C above it
comments.spec_quote: 3.3.2 In heating, the discharge air temperature setpoint shall be reset from the zone temperature up to 20 °F above the zone temperature as the heating loop rises from 0 to 50 percent
comments.reason: The submittal states a rise of 11.1 °C (20 °F) while the specification states a rise of 20 °F.

comments.submittal_quote: With a setpoint above zero, airflow under 70 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes sets a Level 3 low airflow alarm, and airflow under 50 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes sets a Level 2 alarm.
comments.spec_quote: If the measured airflow is below 70 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes while the setpoint is above zero, a Level 3 low airflow alarm shall be set; if it is below 50 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes, a Level 2 alarm shall be set.
comments.reason: The submittal describes the alarm conditions as 'airflow under 70 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes sets a Level 3 low airflow alarm, and airflow under 50 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes sets a Level 2 alarm', while the specification states that the alarm is triggered when airflow is below 70 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes *while the setpoint is above zero*.

comments.submittal_quote: When heating hot water is available, a discharge air temperature 8.3 °C under its setpoint for 10 minutes sets a Level 3 low discharge temperature alarm.
comments.spec_quote: If heating hot water is available and the discharge air temperature is 15 °F below its setpoint for 10 minutes, a Level 3 low discharge temperature alarm shall be set.
comments.reason: The submittal states a temperature difference of 8.3 °C, which converts to 46.3 °F. The specification requires a temperature difference of 15 °F.

comments.spec_quote: 3.4.3 If the damper is commanded closed and the measured airflow stays above 10 percent of the maximum cooling airflow for 10 minutes, a Level 4 leaking damper alarm shall be set.
comments.reason: The specification requires a Level 4 leaking damper alarm when a closed damper maintains airflow above 10% of the maximum cooling airflow for 10 minutes, but the submittal does not include this alarm.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.1.1 Each zone holds 21.7 °C heating and 24.4 °C cooling when occupied and 15.6 °C heating and 29.4 °C cooling when unoccupied.
comments.spec_quote: 3.1.1 Occupied zone setpoints shall be 71 °F heating and 76 °F cooling; unoccupied setpoints shall be 60 °F heating and 85 °F cooling.
comments.reason: The submittal specifies 21.7 °C and 24.4 °C for occupied zones, which is significantly different from the specification's 71 °F and 76 °F.  This represents a conversion error.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.1.2 Occupants may adjust the zone setpoints by at most 1.1 °C in either direction.
comments.spec_quote: 3.1.2 Occupant adjustment of the zone setpoints shall be limited to plus or minus 2 °F.
comments.reason: The submittal specifies a maximum adjustment of 1.1 °C, while the specification requires a maximum adjustment of 2 °F. This represents a conversion error.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.3.1 As the cooling loop rises from 0 to 100 percent, the airflow setpoint rises from the minimum to the maximum cooling airflow.
comments.spec_quote: 3.3.1 In cooling, the airflow setpoint shall be reset from the minimum airflow up to the maximum cooling airflow as the cooling loop rises from 0 to 100 percent.
comments.reason: The submittal states the airflow rises from minimum to maximum as the cooling loop rises, while the specification states the airflow rises from minimum to maximum as the cooling loop rises from 0 to 100 percent. This is a different description of the same behavior.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.3.2 From 0 to 50 percent heating loop the discharge air temperature setpoint rises from zone temperature to 11.1 °C above it
comments.spec_quote: 3.3.2 In heating, the discharge air temperature setpoint shall be reset from the zone temperature up to 20 °F above the zone temperature as the heating loop rises from 0 to 50 percent, and the airflow setpoint shall rise to the maximum heating airflow as the heating loop rises from 50 to 100 percent.
comments.reason: The submittal states the temperature reset is 11.1 °C (20 °F), while the specification requires 20 °F.

comments.submittal_quote: With a setpoint above zero, airflow under 70 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes sets a Level 3 low airflow alarm, and airflow under 50 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes sets a Level 2 alarm.
comments.spec_quote: If the measured airflow is below 70 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes while the setpoint is above zero, a Level 3 low airflow alarm shall be set; if it is below 50 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes, a Level 2 alarm shall be set.
comments.reason: The submittal describes the alarm conditions as 'airflow under 70 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes sets a Level 3 low airflow alarm, and airflow under 50 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes sets a Level 2 alarm', while the specification states 'If the measured airflow is below 70 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes while the setpoint is above zero, a Level 3 low airflow alarm shall be set; if it is below 50 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes, a Level 2 alarm shall be set.' The wording is identical, but the submittal uses a more conversational tone.

comments.submittal_quote: When heating hot water is available, a discharge air temperature 8.3 °C under its setpoint for 10 minutes sets a Level 3 low discharge temperature alarm.
comments.spec_quote: If heating hot water is available and the discharge air temperature is 15 °F below its setpoint for 10 minutes, a Level 3 low discharge temperature alarm shall be set.
comments.reason: The submittal states a temperature difference of 8.3 °C (15 °F), while the specification requires a temperature difference of 15 °F. This is a conversion error.

comments.spec_quote: If the damper is commanded closed and the measured airflow stays above 10 percent of the maximum cooling airflow for 10 minutes, a Level 4 leaking damper alarm shall be set.
comments.reason: The specification requires a Level 4 leaking damper alarm when a closed damper maintains airflow above 10% of the maximum cooling airflow for 10 minutes, but the submittal does not include this alarm.

comments.spec_quote: 3.1.3 The duct static pressure setpoint shall be reset by trim and respond logic between 0.15 in. w.c. and 1.8 in. w.c., starting from 1 in. w.c..

comments.submittal_quote: 3.1.4 At 2 minute intervals the logic lowers the setpoint by 0.05 in. w.c. if there are fewer than 2 zone pressure requests, and otherwise raises it by 0.06 in. w.c. per request beyond 2, limited to 0.15 in. w.c. per interval.
comments.spec_quote: 3.1.4 Every 2 minutes the setpoint shall be trimmed by 0.05 in. w.c. when fewer than 2 zone pressure requests are present, and raised by 0.06 in. w.c. for each request above that number, up to 0.15 in. w.c. per interval.
comments.reason: The submittal states the trim is 0.05 in. w.c. when fewer than 2 zone pressure requests are present, and raises it by 0.06 in. w.c. for each request above that number, up to 0.15 in. w.c. per interval. This is a difference in wording.

comments.submittal_quote: The supply air temperature loop is enabled only while the supply fan is proven on. When it is disabled, heating is off and the economizer is at minimum position.
comments.spec_quote: The supply air temperature control loop shall be enabled when the supply fan is proven on; otherwise the loop shall be disabled with heating off and the economizer at minimum position.
comments.reason: The submittal states the loop is enabled *only* when the supply fan is on, while the specification states it can be disabled with heating off and the economizer at minimum position, creating a contradiction.

comments.submittal_quote: In the Occupied and Setup modes the supply air temperature setpoint is 55 °F with outdoor air at 70 °F or warmer and rises linearly to the maximum setpoint with outdoor air at 60 °F or cooler.
comments.spec_quote: During Occupied and Setup modes the supply air temperature setpoint shall be reset from 55 °F when the outdoor air temperature is 70 °F and above, proportionally up to the maximum supply air temperature setpoint when the outdoor air temperature is 60 °F and below.
comments.reason: The submittal states a linear rise from 55°F to the maximum setpoint when the outdoor air temperature is 60°F and below, while the specification states the rise is proportional to the outdoor air temperature.

comments.submittal_quote: Economizer operation is locked out above an outdoor air temperature of 70 °F and released once the outdoor air temperature drops 1 °F below the limit.
comments.spec_quote: The economizer shall be disabled when the outdoor air temperature exceeds 70 °F and enabled again when it falls 1 °F below that limit.
comments.reason: The submittal states the economizer is locked out above 70°F and released when it drops 1°F, while the specification states it is disabled above 70°F and re-enabled when it drops 1°F. This is a different trigger.

comments.submittal_quote: Stage 1: when supply air temperature stays below 40 °F for 5 minutes, the controller sends two heating hot water plant requests, holds the outdoor air damper at minimum position and modulates the heating coil to maintain at least 42 °F; stage 1 ends after the supply air temperature is above 45 °F for 5 minutes.
comments.spec_quote: If the supply air temperature drops below 40 °F for 5 minutes, the controller shall send two heating hot water plant requests, override the outdoor air damper to minimum position, and modulate the heating coil to keep the supply air temperature at or above 42 °F; this stage shall end when the supply air temperature is above 45 °F for 5 minutes.
comments.reason: The submittal states the outdoor air damper is held at minimum position, while the specification states it is overridden to minimum position. This is a different action.

comments.submittal_quote: The freeze-stat is hardwired in the fan starter circuits and stops the supply and return fans independent of the BAS; the BAS monitors its status.
comments.spec_quote: The freeze-stat shall be hardwired to stop the supply and return fans regardless of the BAS command, and its status shall be monitored by the BAS.
comments.reason: The submittal states the freeze-stat stops the fans independently of the BAS, while the specification states the BAS monitors its status, creating a contradiction in the control logic.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.1.1 Each zone holds 21.1 °C heating and 23.3 °C cooling when occupied and 15.6 °C heating and 29.4 °C cooling when unoccupied.
comments.spec_quote: 3.1.1 Occupied zone setpoints shall be 70 °F heating and 74 °F cooling; unoccupied setpoints shall be 60 °F heating and 85 °F cooling.
comments.reason: The submittal specifies 21.1 °C and 23.3 °C for occupied zones, which is not equivalent to the specification's 70 °F and 74 °F. This represents a significant temperature difference.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.2.1 Each terminal controls its discharge airflow between the scheduled minimum and the active maximum listed below.
comments.spec_quote: 3.2.1 Each terminal shall control discharge airflow between its scheduled minimum airflow and the active maximum airflow listed below.
comments.reason: The submittal states ‘controls its discharge airflow’ while the specification states ‘shall control discharge airflow’.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.3.1 As the cooling loop rises from 0 to 100 percent, the airflow setpoint rises from the minimum to the maximum cooling airflow.
comments.spec_quote: 3.3.1 In cooling, the airflow setpoint shall be reset from the minimum airflow up to the maximum cooling airflow as the cooling loop rises from 0 to 100 percent.
comments.reason: The submittal states the airflow rises from minimum to maximum as the cooling loop rises, while the specification states the airflow rises from minimum to maximum as the cooling loop rises from 0 to 100 percent. This is a different description of the same behavior.

comments.submittal_quote: 3.3.2 From 0 to 50 percent heating loop the discharge air temperature setpoint rises from zone temperature to 11.1 °C above it
comments.spec_quote: 3.3.2 In heating, the discharge air temperature setpoint shall be reset from the zone temperature up to 20 °F above the zone temperature as the heating loop rises from 0 to 50 percent
comments.reason: The submittal states the temperature reset is 11.1 °C (20 °F), while the specification states the temperature reset is 20 °F.

comments.submittal_quote: With a setpoint above zero, airflow under 70 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes sets a Level 3 low airflow alarm, and airflow under 50 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes sets a Level 2 alarm.
comments.spec_quote: If the measured airflow is below 70 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes while the setpoint is above zero, a Level 3 low airflow alarm shall be set; if it is below 50 percent of setpoint for 5 minutes, a Level 2 alarm shall be set.
comments.reason: The submittal describes the alarm conditions differently than the specification, using percentages instead of absolute values.

comments.submittal_quote: When heating hot water is available, a discharge air temperature 8.3 °C under its setpoint for 10 minutes sets a Level 3 low discharge temperature alarm.
comments.spec_quote: If heating hot water is available and the discharge air temperature is 15 °F below its setpoint for 10 minutes, a Level 3 low discharge temperature alarm shall be set.
comments.reason: The submittal states the temperature difference as 8.3 °C while the specification states it as 15 °F.

comments.submittal_quote: Whenever the AHU-8 supply fan is not proven on, heating is disabled and the hot water valve is closed.
comments.spec_quote: The hot water valve shall be closed and heating disabled whenever the AHU-8 supply fan is not proven on.
comments.reason: The submittal states the hot water valve is closed when the fan is not proven on, while the specification states heating is disabled and the valve is closed. This creates a contradiction in the interlock behavior.
